slides.narration: Welcome. In this chapter we study the Parliament of India, the body that makes laws for the whole country. Parliament has three parts: the President, the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha. In this first part we see how powers are shared between the Union and the States, how the Lok Sabha is formed, and why its presiding officer, the Speaker, matters so much.

slides.heading: A federal set-up
slides.body_md: India has **two levels of government**: the **Union** and the **States**. The **Constitution** divides law-making powers between them, so neither can take away the other's powers on its own.
bullets: Written Constitution
Division of powers
Independent courts to settle disputes
slides.narration: India is a federation. There is a government for the whole country, called the Union, and a government in each State. The Constitution itself divides the subjects on which each can make laws. Because the division is written down, neither level can simply take over the other's work, and the courts can settle disputes between them.

slides.narration: The division is made through three lists in the Seventh Schedule. The Union List has subjects of national importance, such as defence and foreign affairs. The State List has subjects of local importance, such as police and agriculture. On the Concurrent List both may make laws, for example education and forests. Any subject not named in any list is a residuary subject, and Parliament makes laws on it.

slides.heading: Quick check: which list?
slides.body_md: Kavya's town needs more police stations. Whose subject is this?
slides.narration: Think about whether the subject is national or local. Then pick the list.

slides.heading: A strong Centre
slides.body_md: The division of powers **favours the Union**.
bullets: The Union List has the most important subjects
Residuary powers belong to the Union
On a Concurrent subject, a Union law generally prevails over a conflicting State law

visual.alt: Table of three situations: unlisted subjects are decided by Parliament, a clash on a Concurrent subject is generally won by the Union law, and State subjects by the State legislature

slides.narration: Although India is federal, the Centre has been made stronger. The most important subjects are in the Union List. Residuary powers belong to the Union. And if a State law and a Union law clash on a Concurrent subject, the Union law generally prevails. This is why India is often described as a federation with a strong Centre.

slides.heading: The Lok Sabha: House of the People
slides.body_md: Members are **directly elected** by adult citizens. Up to **530** from the States and **20** from the Union Territories (maximum **550**); **543** are elected at present.
bullets: Seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Dated note: two Anglo-Indian members were nominated earlier (old maximum 552); this ended with the 104th Amendment in January 2020

rows: elected MLAs; 12 nominated by the President

visual.alt: Comparison table of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha: name, method of choice, maximum size, present strength, minimum age, term and presiding officer
visual.caption: Present strengths as of 2024.

slides.narration: The Lok Sabha is the House of the People. Its members are chosen directly by the voters. Up to five hundred and thirty members come from the States and up to twenty from the Union Territories. At present five hundred and forty-three seats are filled at a general election. Earlier, two members of the Anglo-Indian community were nominated, but that provision ended in January twenty twenty.

slides.heading: Who can become a member?

rows: Not of unsound mind or insolvent

visual.alt: Table of qualifications: both Houses need citizenship, no office of profit and sound mind; the minimum age is 25 for the Lok Sabha and 30 for the Rajya Sabha

slides.narration: To be a member of the Lok Sabha, a person must be a citizen of India and at least twenty-five years old. The person must not hold an office of profit under the government, and must not be of unsound mind or an undischarged insolvent. Notice that the Rajya Sabha needs the same, except that the minimum age there is thirty years.

slides.heading: Quick check: old enough?
slides.body_md: Ritika was born in 2003. From which year can she contest a Lok Sabha election?
slides.narration: Add the minimum age for the Lok Sabha to her year of birth.

slides.heading: The term of the Lok Sabha

nodes.label: Normal term: five years from the first meeting
Shortened: President dissolves on the Prime Minister's advice
Extended in a national emergency: one year at a time
Limit: not beyond six months after the emergency ends

visual.alt: Flow of the Lok Sabha term: normally five years, may be shortened by dissolution, may be extended during a national emergency by one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the emergency ends
visual.caption: Term of the Lok Sabha

slides.narration: The Lok Sabha normally lasts five years from its first meeting. It can end earlier if the President dissolves it on the advice of the Prime Minister. During a national emergency, Parliament can extend its life by law, one year at a time, but never beyond six months after the emergency is over.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: dissolution or extension?
slides.body_md: Decide what happens in each imagined case.
bullets: A three-year-old Lok Sabha faces a fresh election → it was **dissolved early**
An emergency is in force when the term ends → Parliament may **extend** it by one year
The emergency ends; the House is now 6½ years old → it must end **within six months** of the emergency's end

rows: Dissolution by the President on advice
Extension by law, one year at a time
No more than six months beyond it

visual.alt: Worked table of three cases: an early election means dissolution, an emergency at the end of the term allows extension by one year at a time, and after the emergency ends the House can last at most six more months

slides.narration: Let us apply the rules. If a Lok Sabha only three years old faces an election, it must have been dissolved early. If an emergency is in force when its five years end, Parliament may extend it by one year at a time. Once the emergency is over, the House can continue for at most six more months.

slides.heading: The Speaker
slides.body_md: The **presiding officer** of the Lok Sabha. Elected by the **members from among themselves**; holds office for the **life of the House**.

nodes.label: Members elect a Speaker from among themselves
Speaker presides for the life of the House
Continues till the next House first meets

visual.alt: Flow of the Speaker's tenure: a new Lok Sabha meets, members elect a Speaker from among themselves, the Speaker presides for the life of the House and continues until the next House first meets
visual.caption: Election and tenure of the Speaker

slides.narration: The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha. The members elect the Speaker from among themselves, usually soon after a new House first meets. The Speaker stays in office for the life of that House, and even after the House is dissolved, continues until just before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha, so the office is never empty.

slides.heading: Removing the Speaker

nodes.label: At least 14 days' notice of a resolution
Vote: majority of all the then members

visual.alt: Flow of the removal of the Speaker: fourteen days' notice, debate with the Speaker not presiding, vote by a majority of all the then members, then the office falls vacant
visual.caption: Removal of the Speaker

slides.narration: Removing a Speaker is deliberately difficult. Members must give at least fourteen days notice of a resolution. While it is discussed, the Speaker does not preside, though the Speaker may speak and vote. The resolution passes only with a majority of all the then members of the House, which is called an effective majority.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: an effective majority
slides.body_md: The House has 543 seats and 7 are vacant. How many votes remove the Speaker?

visual.alt: Worked table: 543 seats minus 7 vacancies gives 536 members; a majority of them is 269
visual.caption: Imagined figures.

slides.narration: Here is a worked example with imagined figures. Start with the seats, five hundred and forty-three. Subtract the seven vacant seats to get five hundred and thirty-six members. A majority of them is more than half, which is two hundred and sixty-nine votes. Fewer votes than that, even if they outnumber the votes against, do not remove the Speaker.

slides.heading: Functions of the Speaker

rows: conducts business, decides who speaks, keeps order
certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill; decision final
votes only to break a tie
presides when both Houses sit together
adjourns the House if one-tenth of members are not present

visual.alt: Table of five functions of the Speaker: presiding, certifying Money Bills, casting vote, presiding over joint sittings and adjourning the House for want of quorum

slides.narration: The Speaker conducts the business of the House, decides who speaks and keeps order. The Speaker certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill, and that decision is final. The Speaker votes only to break a tie, presides over joint sittings of both Houses, and adjourns the House if one-tenth of the members are not present.

slides.heading: Quick check: a tied vote
slides.body_md: A vote in the Lok Sabha is tied. What does the Speaker do?
slides.narration: Remember when the Speaker votes.

slides.heading: Quick check: after dissolution
slides.body_md: The Lok Sabha is dissolved in March. Who is Speaker in April?
slides.narration: Think about why the office should never be empty.

Speaker: elected by members; removed by an effective majority after 14 days' notice; casting vote; certifies Money Bills

slides.narration: To sum up Part 1. Powers are divided by three lists, and the Centre is stronger. The Lok Sabha is directly elected, has five hundred and forty-three elected members at present, needs a minimum age of twenty-five, and lasts five years. The Speaker is elected by the members, is hard to remove, votes only in a tie and certifies Money Bills.

decks.title: The Union Parliament — Part 2: The Rajya Sabha
goals: Describe the composition of the Rajya Sabha and how its members are chosen
Explain why the Rajya Sabha is a permanent House
Compare the two Houses and plan a 10-mark answer

slides.heading: The Rajya Sabha: Council of States
slides.body_md: Part 2 — composition, election, term and Presiding Officer of the **Rajya Sabha**.

rows: elected MLAs; 12 nominated by the President

visual.alt: Comparison table of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha: name, method of choice, maximum size, present strength, minimum age, term and presiding officer
visual.caption: Present strengths as of 2024.

slides.narration: In Part 2 we study the Rajya Sabha, the Council of States. It differs from the Lok Sabha in how its members are chosen, how long they serve, and who presides over it. Keep the comparison table in mind as we go through each point.

slides.heading: Composition
slides.body_md: Maximum **250**: up to **238** representatives of the States and Union Territories and **12** members **nominated by the President**. Present strength **245** (as of 2024).
bullets: Seats are shared among the States roughly by population
Nominated members: special knowledge in literature, science, art and social service

visual.alt: Table: up to 238 representatives of States and Union Territories plus 12 nominated, a maximum of 250

slides.narration: The Rajya Sabha can have at most two hundred and fifty members. Up to two hundred and thirty-eight represent the States and Union Territories, and twelve are nominated by the President for their special knowledge in literature, science, art and social service. Its present strength is two hundred and forty-five.

slides.heading: How members are chosen

visual.alt: Flow: voters elect MLAs, the elected MLAs elect Rajya Sabha members by proportional representation with the single transferable vote, and the President nominates twelve more
visual.caption: How the Rajya Sabha is chosen

slides.narration: Rajya Sabha members are not chosen by the voters directly. The voters elect members of the State Legislative Assemblies, and these elected members then choose the State's representatives in the Rajya Sabha, using proportional representation with the single transferable vote. The President adds twelve nominated members.

slides.heading: Quick check: how did she get there?
slides.body_md: A classical dancer joins the Rajya Sabha without contesting any election. How?
slides.narration: Recall who the twelve nominated members are.

slides.heading: Qualifications and term
bullets: Citizen of India
At least 30 years of age
Six-year term for each member

rows: Not of unsound mind or insolvent

visual.alt: Table of qualifications: both Houses need citizenship, no office of profit and sound mind; the minimum age is 25 for the Lok Sabha and 30 for the Rajya Sabha

slides.narration: A member of the Rajya Sabha must be a citizen of India and at least thirty years old, with the same disqualifications as for the Lok Sabha. Each member serves for six years, which is one year longer than the normal life of a Lok Sabha.

sections.heading: 1. Parliament and the federal set-up
sections.body_md:
Parliament consists of the **President**, the **Rajya Sabha** and the **Lok Sabha**. India is a **federation**: the Constitution divides law-making powers between the Union and the States through three lists in the **Seventh Schedule**.

- **Union List:** subjects of national importance, e.g. defence, foreign affairs, railways, banking.
- **State List:** subjects of local importance, e.g. police and public order, agriculture, public health.
- **Concurrent List:** both may legislate, e.g. education, forests, marriage, trade unions. In a clash, the **Union law generally prevails**.
- **Residuary powers** (subjects in no list) belong to **Parliament**.

key_terms.definition_md: A system with two levels of government whose powers are divided by a written constitution.
Power to make laws on subjects not mentioned in any list; in India it belongs to Parliament.

sections.heading: 2. The Lok Sabha: composition
sections.body_md:
The **House of the People**, elected **directly** by adult citizens. Up to **530** members from the States and **20** from the Union Territories (maximum **550**); **543** are elected at present. Seats are **reserved** for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

**Dated note:** until January 2020 the President could nominate two members of the Anglo-Indian community, making the maximum 552; the 104th Amendment (2020) did not extend this, so no members are nominated now.

sections.heading: 3. The Lok Sabha: qualifications and term
sections.body_md:
**Qualifications:** citizen of India; at least **25 years**; name on an electoral roll; must not hold an **office of profit** under the government; must not be of unsound mind or an undischarged insolvent.

**Term:** five years from the first meeting. It may be **dissolved earlier** by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. During a **national emergency** Parliament may extend it by law, **one year at a time**, but not beyond **six months after the emergency** ends.

Ending the life of the Lok Sabha so that a fresh general election is held.

sections.heading: 4. The Speaker
sections.body_md:
**Election:** by the members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves. **Tenure:** the life of the House; continues after dissolution until just before the first meeting of the new House.

**Removal:** a resolution after at least **14 days' notice**, passed by a **majority of all the then members** (effective majority); the Speaker does not preside during it but may speak and vote.

**Functions:** presides and keeps order; certifies **Money Bills** (final); **casting vote** in a tie; presides over **joint sittings**; adjourns the House if the **quorum** of one-tenth is not present. The **Deputy Speaker** presides in the Speaker's absence.

key_terms.definition_md: A majority of all the then members of the House, that is total seats minus vacancies.
A vote given by the presiding officer only to break a tie.

sections.heading: 5. The Rajya Sabha
sections.body_md:
**Composition:** maximum **250** = up to **238** representatives of the States and Union Territories + **12** nominated by the President (literature, science, art, social service). Present strength **245** (as of 2024).

**Election:** by the **elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies**, by **proportional representation** with the **single transferable vote**.

**Qualifications:** citizen; at least **30 years**; other conditions as for the Lok Sabha. **Term:** six years. It is a **permanent House**: never dissolved; about **one-third retire every second year**.

**Presiding Officer:** the **Vice-President** as ex-officio Chairman; an elected **Deputy Chairman**.

By virtue of holding another office; the Vice-President chairs the Rajya Sabha because of being Vice-President.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Writing 552 as today's Lok Sabha: the maximum is **550** elected since 2020; **543** are elected at present.
- Saying the Speaker is removed by a two-thirds majority: it is a **majority of all the then members** after **14 days' notice**.
- Saying the Rajya Sabha is elected by the people: it is elected by **elected MLAs**.
- Mixing **250** (maximum) and **245** (present) for the Rajya Sabha.

**How marks are usually awarded**
- 1 mark: one correct option or term.
- 2 marks: two clear points.
- 10 marks: three parts (3 + 3 + 4), one point per mark.

A paid government post that **disqualifies** a person from membership.
The **members of the Lok Sabha**, from among themselves.
Continues **until just before the first meeting** of the new House.
**14 days' notice**; **majority of all the then members**.
Majority of all the **then members** (seats minus vacancies).

cards.front_md: Who decides if a bill is a Money Bill?
Who presides over a joint sitting?

cards.back_md: **Elected MLAs**, by proportional representation (single transferable vote).

cards.front_md: Term of a Rajya Sabha member
Presiding Officer of the Rajya Sabha

cards.back_md: Never dissolved; members retire in **batches** every two years.

questions.stem_md: Which feature of the Indian Constitution shows that India has a **federal** set-up?

options.text_md: The President is elected indirectly
Powers are divided between the Union and the States by the Constitution
There is a single citizenship for the whole country
All High Courts work under one Supreme Court

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** Powers are divided between the Union and the States by the Constitution. A federation divides powers between two levels of government by a written constitution. Single citizenship and an integrated judiciary are unitary features, and the method of electing the President does not decide federalism.

questions.stem_md: Kavya's town wants more police stations to deal with rising thefts. Under the division of powers, **police and public order** are subjects of the

options.text_md: Union List
Concurrent List
residuary powers of the Union
State List

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** State List. Police and public order are State subjects, so the State government decides. Defence and railways are Union subjects; education and forests are Concurrent.

questions.stem_md: Both Parliament and the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly pass laws on the same subject. Which subject is it most likely to be?

options.text_md: Education
Defence
Foreign affairs
Agriculture

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** Education. Education is on the Concurrent List, where both levels may make laws. Defence and foreign affairs are Union subjects; agriculture is a State subject.

questions.stem_md: A new subject such as regulating space tourism is not mentioned in any of the three lists. Who can make laws on it?

options.text_md: Only the State where the launch site lies
Any State that passes a law first
Parliament, because residuary powers belong to the Union
Only the Supreme Court

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Parliament, because residuary powers belong to the Union. Subjects not listed anywhere are residuary subjects, and the power to make laws on them belongs to Parliament. Courts do not make such laws, and States have no residuary power.

questions.stem_md: An imagined State law on trade unions conflicts with a law made by Parliament on the same Concurrent subject. In general, which law prevails?

options.text_md: The State law, because the State is closer to the people
The law passed later
The law made by Parliament
Neither; both lapse

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** The law made by Parliament. On a Concurrent subject, the Union law generally prevails over a conflicting State law, to the extent of the conflict. Being passed later does not by itself decide the matter.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Defence and foreign affairs are placed in the Union List.

**Reason (R):** Subjects of national importance that need a uniform policy for the whole country are given to the Union.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: (A) is true and (R) is false.
(A) is false and (R) is true.
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Both are true, and R gives the reason for A: defence and relations with other countries need one policy for all of India.

questions.stem_md: True or false? The three lists that divide legislative powers between the Union and the States are found in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md: **True.** The Union, State and Concurrent Lists are in the Seventh Schedule.

questions.stem_md: Match each subject that came up in an imagined Class 10 quiz at Kohima with the list it belongs to.

options.text_md: Railways
Public health and hospitals
Forests
A subject not named in any list

questions.solution_md: **Key:** (a)–(r), (b)–(p), (c)–(s), (d)–(q). Railways are a Union subject; public health is a State subject; forests are Concurrent; unlisted subjects fall under the residuary power of Parliament.

questions.stem_md: Name the three lists that divide law-making powers in India and give one subject from each.
questions.solution_md: Three lists with one correct subject each; all three needed for full marks.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. **Union List**, e.g. defence. 2. **State List**, e.g. police. 3. **Concurrent List**, e.g. education. (Any correct example in each.)

questions.stem_md: What is meant by the Concurrent List, and why does a Union law usually prevail in case of conflict on it?
questions.solution_md: Meaning of the list and the reason for Union supremacy on it.

answer.model_answer_md: The **Concurrent List** contains subjects on which **both Parliament and State legislatures** can make laws. A Union law usually prevails so that there is **one uniform rule** for the whole country on matters of common interest.

questions.stem_md: Give three features of the division of powers that show the Union has been made stronger than the States.
questions.solution_md: Any three valid features of Union predominance in the division of powers.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. The **Union List** has the most important subjects, such as defence and currency. 2. **Residuary powers** belong to the Union. 3. On a **Concurrent** subject, a Union law generally **prevails** over a conflicting State law.

questions.stem_md: Members of the Lok Sabha are chosen by

options.text_md: the voters of the country through direct election
the members of the State Legislative Assemblies
the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
the Election Commission from a list of candidates

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** the voters of the country through direct election. The Lok Sabha is the House of the People, elected directly by adult citizens. State legislators elect Rajya Sabha members; the President nominates only a few Rajya Sabha members.

questions.stem_md: Ritika, a citizen of India, was born in 2003. From which year onward is she old enough to contest a Lok Sabha election?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** 2028. The minimum age for the Lok Sabha is 25 years, so 2003 + 25 = 2028. Eighteen is the voting age, and 30 is the age for the Rajya Sabha.

questions.stem_md: The normal term of the Lok Sabha is

options.text_md: six years from the date of election
five years from the date of its first meeting
four years from the date of its first meeting
until every member retires

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** five years from the date of its first meeting. The Lok Sabha has a term of five years from its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier. Six years is the term of a Rajya Sabha member.

questions.stem_md: In an imagined year the Lok Sabha is only three years old when a new general election is held. What is the most likely reason?

options.text_md: The President dissolved the Lok Sabha early on the advice of the Prime Minister
The Rajya Sabha voted to end its term
One-third of its members retired
The Speaker resigned

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** The President dissolved the Lok Sabha early on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Lok Sabha can be dissolved before five years by the President, on the advice of the Prime Minister. One-third retirement applies to the Rajya Sabha, and the Speaker's resignation does not end the House.

questions.stem_md: During a national emergency, the term of the Lok Sabha can be extended by Parliament

options.text_md: for any period it chooses
by up to one year at a time, and not beyond six months after the emergency ends
by five years at a time
only with the approval of every State

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** by up to one year at a time, and not beyond six months after the emergency ends. An extension during an emergency is by law for up to one year at a time, and cannot continue beyond six months after the emergency has ended.

questions.stem_md: How many members are elected to the Lok Sabha at a general election at present?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** 543. At present 543 members are elected. 552 was the older maximum including two nominated members; 245 and 250 relate to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.stem_md: Arjun, a 32-year-old citizen, works as a paid officer of a State government department and wants to contest a Lok Sabha seat. What stands in his way?

options.text_md: He is too young for the Lok Sabha
He is not a member of a political party
He has never been elected to a State Assembly
He holds an office of profit under a government

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** He holds an office of profit under a government. A person holding an office of profit under the Union or a State government (other than offices exempted by law) cannot be a member. He is old enough (25 is the minimum), and party membership or earlier experience is not required.

questions.stem_md: Why are some Lok Sabha constituencies reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.text_md: Because only members of these communities may vote in them
Because these seats are filled by nomination
Because their members serve for six years
To ensure these communities have a fair share of representation in Parliament

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** To ensure these communities have a fair share of representation in Parliament. In a reserved constituency only candidates from the community may contest, but all voters of the constituency vote. The aim is fair representation; the seats are elected, and the term is the same.

questions.stem_md: A candidate for the Lok Sabha must be at least ___ years of age.
questions.solution_md: The minimum age is 25 years.

questions.stem_md: The Constitution allows up to 530 members of the Lok Sabha from the States and up to 20 from the Union Territories. What is the maximum number of elected members?
questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Add the two limits.
Step 2: 530 + 20 = 550 members.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Lok Sabha is called the House of the People.

**Reason (R):** Its members are elected directly by the adult citizens of India.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: (A) is true and (R) is false.
(A) is false and (R) is true.
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Both are true, and R explains A: direct election by the people is why it is called the House of the People.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Two members of the Lok Sabha are still nominated by the President to represent the Anglo-Indian community.

**Reason (R):** The provision for nominating Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha was not extended beyond January 2020.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: (A) is true and (R) is false.
(A) is false and (R) is true.
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** A is false: since the 104th Amendment (2020) no members are nominated to the Lok Sabha. R is true.

questions.stem_md: True or false? The Lok Sabha is a permanent House that is never dissolved.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md: **False.** The Lok Sabha is dissolved at the end of its term or earlier; it is the Rajya Sabha that is permanent.

questions.stem_md: State any two qualifications required to become a member of the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution_md: Any two correct qualifications.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. Must be a **citizen of India**. 2. Must be at least **25 years** of age. (Also: name on an electoral roll; must not hold an office of profit; must not be of unsound mind or an undischarged insolvent.)

questions.stem_md: Describe the composition of the Lok Sabha as it stands after the 104th Amendment (2020).
questions.solution_md: Elected limits for States and UTs, present strength, and the end of nomination.

answer.model_answer_md: Up to **530 members** elected from the States and up to **20** from the Union Territories (maximum **550**); at present **543** are elected. **No members are nominated** any longer, since the two Anglo-Indian seats ended in 2020.

questions.stem_md: In what two ways can the five-year term of the Lok Sabha be changed?
questions.solution_md: Early dissolution and extension during an emergency.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. It can be **shortened** when the President **dissolves** it early on the advice of the Prime Minister. 2. It can be **extended** by Parliament during a **national emergency**, by one year at a time and not beyond six months after the emergency ends.

marking_scheme.step: Extension during an emergency with its limit

questions.stem_md: Why is the Lok Sabha considered more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in a parliamentary democracy? Give three reasons.
questions.solution_md: Three distinct reasons linked to election, responsibility and money matters.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. It is **directly elected** by the people, so it speaks for them. 2. The **Council of Ministers is responsible** to it; a no-confidence motion can be passed only there. 3. **Money Bills** start only in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha can delay them only for 14 days.

questions.stem_md: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is

options.text_md: appointed by the President
elected by both Houses together
elected by the members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves
the senior-most member of the ruling party

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** elected by the members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves. The Lok Sabha elects its own Speaker from among its members. The President does not appoint the Speaker, and the Rajya Sabha has no role.

questions.stem_md: A resolution to remove the Speaker must be passed by

options.text_md: a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, without notice
a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha, after at least 14 days' notice
a simple majority of members present, after 7 days' notice
both Houses of Parliament in a joint sitting

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha, after at least 14 days' notice. Removal needs an effective majority (a majority of all the then members) and at least fourteen days' notice of the resolution.

questions.stem_md: On a bill in the Lok Sabha, 250 members vote for and 250 against. What does the Speaker do?

options.text_md: Exercises a casting vote to decide the matter
Votes along with the ruling party in the first instance
Sends the bill to the President
Asks the Rajya Sabha to decide

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** Exercises a casting vote to decide the matter. The Speaker does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote in case of a tie. The bill is not sent to the President or the Rajya Sabha to break a tie.

questions.stem_md: If a question arises whether a bill is a Money Bill, whose decision is final?

options.text_md: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Finance Minister
The Prime Minister

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** The Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Under the Constitution the certificate of the Speaker on this question cannot be challenged. The Rajya Sabha Chairman, the Finance Minister and the Prime Minister have no such power.

questions.stem_md: The Lok Sabha is dissolved in March, and the new House first meets in June. Who is the Speaker in April?

options.text_md: No one, because the office ends with dissolution
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The senior-most member of the dissolved House
The same Speaker, who stays in office until just before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** The same Speaker, who stays in office until just before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha. The Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution but continues until immediately before the first meeting of the new House.

questions.stem_md: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament?

options.text_md: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Vice-President
The President
The Prime Minister

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** The Speaker of the Lok Sabha. The Speaker presides over a joint sitting. The Vice-President presides over the Rajya Sabha, not over joint sittings.

questions.stem_md: During a debate in the Lok Sabha, a member keeps shouting and refuses to take his seat. What can the Speaker do?

options.text_md: Dismiss him from the Lok Sabha permanently
Ask the President to dissolve the House
Order the member to withdraw or suspend him for the day, and adjourn the House if needed
Remove his name from the electoral roll

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Order the member to withdraw or suspend him for the day, and adjourn the House if needed. Maintaining order is the Speaker's duty: the Speaker can name, suspend or ask a member to withdraw, and adjourn the House in grave disorder. Membership is not ended this way.

questions.stem_md: In an imagined year the Lok Sabha has 543 seats, of which 7 are vacant. What is the smallest number of votes needed to pass a resolution removing the Speaker?
questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Then members = 543 − 7 = 536.
Step 2: A majority of 536 is more than half: 536 ÷ 2 = 268, so 269 votes.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Speaker does not vote in the first instance on ordinary matters.

**Reason (R):** The Speaker is not a member of the Lok Sabha.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: (A) is true and (R) is false.
(A) is false and (R) is true.
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** A is true: the Speaker votes only to break a tie. R is false: the Speaker is an elected member of the Lok Sabha.

questions.stem_md: True or false? In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md: **True.** The Deputy Speaker, also elected by the House, presides when the Speaker is absent.

questions.stem_md: A resolution to remove the Speaker can be moved only after at least ___ days' notice.
questions.solution_md: Fourteen days' notice is required.

questions.stem_md: Put the steps in removing the Speaker of the Lok Sabha in the correct order.

options.text_md: The Speaker vacates office
Members give at least fourteen days' notice of a resolution for removal
The resolution is passed by a majority of all the then members
The resolution is taken up while the Speaker does not preside but may speak and vote

questions.solution_md: **Correct order:** (b) → (d) → (c) → (a). Notice comes first, then debate with the Speaker not presiding, then the vote by an effective majority, and finally the office falls vacant.

marking_scheme.step: Complete correct sequence (all items in place)

questions.stem_md: Mention any two functions of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution_md: Any two correct functions.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. **Presides** over the Lok Sabha and **maintains order**. 2. **Certifies Money Bills**; the decision is final. (Also: casting vote in a tie; presides over joint sittings; adjourns the House when there is no quorum.)

questions.stem_md: Explain why the Speaker continues in office even after the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
questions.solution_md: Rule plus the reason (continuity).

answer.model_answer_md: The Speaker stays until **just before the first meeting of the new House**, so that there is **no gap** in the office: someone is there to look after the **Secretariat** and the work of the Lok Sabha until a new Speaker is elected.

marking_scheme.step: Rule: until the first meeting of the new House

questions.stem_md: In an imagined case, 262 members vote for a resolution to remove the Speaker and 190 against, when the House has 536 members (seats minus vacancies). Is the Speaker removed? Give a reason.
questions.solution_md: Apply the effective-majority rule to the numbers.

answer.model_answer_md: **No.** Removal needs a majority of **all the then members**, that is at least **269** of 536. Only **262** voted for it, so the resolution fails even though more members voted for it than against.

questions.stem_md: The Speaker is usually elected from the ruling side but is expected to be impartial. Give three features of the office that help the Speaker act impartially.
questions.solution_md: Three distinct safeguards of impartiality.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. The Speaker **does not vote** in the first instance, only to break a tie. 2. **Removal** needs an **effective majority** with **14 days' notice**, so the Speaker cannot be removed easily. 3. The Speaker's **salary** is charged on the Consolidated Fund and the Speaker's rulings on procedure cannot be questioned in the House.

questions.stem_md: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha laid down in the Constitution is

options.text_md: 245: all elected
550: all elected
250: 238 representatives of the States and Union Territories and 12 nominated
250: all nominated by the President

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** 250: 238 representatives of the States and Union Territories and 12 nominated. The maximum is 250: up to 238 elected representatives and 12 members nominated by the President. 245 is the present strength.

questions.stem_md: Representatives of a State in the Rajya Sabha are elected by

options.text_md: the elected members of that State's Legislative Assembly, by proportional representation with the single transferable vote
the voters of the State directly
the Lok Sabha members from that State
the Governor of the State

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** the elected members of that State's Legislative Assembly, by proportional representation with the single transferable vote. State representatives are chosen by the elected MLAs of the State using proportional representation by the single transferable vote.

questions.stem_md: An imagined classical dancer from Odisha with no party connection becomes a member of the Rajya Sabha without contesting any election. How is this possible?

options.text_md: She won the most votes in her State
The Speaker appointed her
She was chosen by lot
The President nominated her for her special knowledge or experience in art

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** The President nominated her for her special knowledge or experience in art. The President nominates twelve members with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

questions.stem_md: Why is the Rajya Sabha called a permanent House?

options.text_md: Its members are appointed for life
It is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every second year
It meets every day of the year
It cannot be adjourned

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** It is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every second year. The Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution. About one-third of the members retire every two years, so the House continues while its membership changes.

questions.stem_md: The Presiding Officer of the Rajya Sabha is

options.text_md: the Vice-President of India, as ex-officio Chairman
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
the senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha
the Chief Justice of India

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** the Vice-President of India, as ex-officio Chairman. The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; the Deputy Chairman is elected by the members.

questions.stem_md: Dev, a citizen of India, turns 28 this year. Which of these can he contest now?

options.text_md: A Rajya Sabha seat, but not a Lok Sabha seat
A Lok Sabha seat, but not a Rajya Sabha seat
Both Houses
Neither House

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** A Lok Sabha seat, but not a Rajya Sabha seat. The minimum age is 25 for the Lok Sabha and 30 for the Rajya Sabha, so at 28 he qualifies only for the Lok Sabha.

questions.stem_md: Study the picture of two Houses, P and Q. Which House is the Rajya Sabha, and which feature in the picture shows it?

options.text_md: P, because it is the larger House
Q, because it has no nominated members
Q, because it has members nominated by the President besides members elected by State legislators
P, because its members are elected by State legislators

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Q, because it has members nominated by the President besides members elected by State legislators. House Q has up to 238 members elected by State legislators and 12 nominated by the President, which is the Rajya Sabha. House P, directly elected with no nominated members, is the Lok Sabha.

questions.stem_md: Meera was elected to the Rajya Sabha in 2026 for a full term. In which year will her term end?
questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** 2032. A Rajya Sabha member has a six-year term: 2026 + 6 = 2032.

questions.stem_md: The President nominates ___ members to the Rajya Sabha.
questions.solution_md: Twelve members are nominated.

questions.stem_md: True or false? The President can dissolve the Rajya Sabha on the advice of the Prime Minister.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md: **False.** The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and cannot be dissolved; only the Lok Sabha can be.

questions.stem_md: An imagined member is elected to the Rajya Sabha in 2026 for a full term and is not re-elected. In which year does the member's term end?
questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The term is 6 years.
Step 2: 2026 + 6 = 2032.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Rajya Sabha is called the Council of States.

**Reason (R):** The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: (A) is true and (R) is false.
(A) is false and (R) is true.
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** Both are true, but R does not explain A. It is called the Council of States because its members represent the States, being elected by the State legislatures.

questions.stem_md: Match each feature with the House of Parliament or office it describes, as an imagined civics club at Shillong sorted them.

options.text_md: Permanent House; one-third retire every second year
Term of five years unless dissolved earlier
Presides over joint sittings of both Houses
Ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States

questions.solution_md: **Key:** (a)–(s), (b)–(q), (c)–(r), (d)–(p). Rotation belongs to the Rajya Sabha; the five-year term to the Lok Sabha; the Speaker presides at joint sittings; the Vice-President chairs the Rajya Sabha.

questions.stem_md: Explain why the Rajya Sabha is said to be a permanent House.
questions.solution_md: No dissolution plus the rotation of members.

answer.model_answer_md: It is **never dissolved** as a whole. Members serve **six years**, and about **one-third retire every second year**, with new members elected in their place, so the House continues without a break.

marking_scheme.step: Six-year terms with one-third retiring every two years

questions.stem_md: State two qualifications for membership of the Rajya Sabha that differ from or match those for the Lok Sabha.
questions.solution_md: Citizenship and the age of 30, with the comparison.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. Must be a **citizen of India** (same as for the Lok Sabha). 2. Must be at least **30 years** of age (the Lok Sabha needs 25).

questions.stem_md: Why does the Constitution allow the President to nominate twelve members to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution_md: Who is nominated and the benefit to Parliament.

answer.model_answer_md: To bring into Parliament people with **special knowledge or practical experience** in **literature, science, art and social service**, who may not wish to contest elections. Their expertise **improves the quality of debate**.

questions.stem_md: Who presides over the Rajya Sabha, and who takes the chair in that person's absence?
questions.solution_md: Chairman and Deputy Chairman.

answer.model_answer_md: The **Vice-President** of India presides as **ex-officio Chairman**. In the Chairman's absence the **Deputy Chairman**, elected by the members of the Rajya Sabha, presides.

questions.stem_md: Give three ways in which the Rajya Sabha protects the interests of the States in the federal system.
questions.solution_md: Three roles connected with the States.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. Its members are **elected by the State legislatures**, so they speak for the States. 2. It can pass a resolution letting Parliament make laws on a **State List** subject in the **national interest**, so such a step needs its consent. 3. It can authorise the creation of new **All-India Services** shared by the Union and the States.

marking_scheme.step: Consent for laws on State subjects

questions.stem_md: Distinguish between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha on any four points.
questions.solution_md: Four points, each with both sides.

answer.model_answer_md: 1. **Election:** Lok Sabha directly by the people; Rajya Sabha by State legislators. 2. **Term:** Lok Sabha five years and can be dissolved; Rajya Sabha permanent, members serve six years. 3. **Age:** 25 for the Lok Sabha; 30 for the Rajya Sabha. 4. **Presiding officer:** the elected Speaker; the Vice-President as Chairman.

questions.stem_md:
With reference to the Lok Sabha, answer the following.

(i) Describe its composition at present. [3]

(ii) State any three qualifications for its membership. [3]

(iii) Explain how its term of five years may be shortened or extended. [4]
questions.solution_md: Composition with numbers and method; three qualifications; dissolution and extension with the limit.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(i)** Up to **530** members elected from the States and up to **20** from the Union Territories (maximum **550**); **543** are elected at present by **direct election**; some seats are **reserved** for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes; no members are nominated since 2020.

**(ii)** A **citizen of India**; at least **25 years** old; not holding an **office of profit** (also: name on an electoral roll; not of unsound mind).

**(iii)** It may be **dissolved early** by the **President** on the advice of the **Prime Minister**, leading to a fresh election. During a **national emergency**, Parliament may **extend** its term by law by **one year at a time**, but not beyond **six months after the emergency** ends.

marking_scheme.step: (i) Elected limits for States and UTs
(iii) On the advice of the Prime Minister
(iii) Extension during an emergency, one year at a time
(iii) Not beyond six months after the emergency

questions.stem_md:
The Speaker is the guardian of the dignity of the Lok Sabha.

(i) How is the Speaker elected, and how long does the Speaker hold office? [3]

(ii) Explain the procedure for removing the Speaker. [3]

(iii) Describe any four functions of the Speaker. [4]
questions.solution_md: Election and tenure; removal procedure with notice and majority; four functions.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(i)** The **members of the Lok Sabha elect** the Speaker **from among themselves**, usually at the first sitting of a new House. The Speaker holds office for the **life of the House** and continues after dissolution **until just before the first meeting** of the new Lok Sabha.

**(ii)** A resolution for removal can be moved after at least **14 days' notice**. It must be passed by a **majority of all the then members** (effective majority). While it is considered, the Speaker **does not preside** but may speak and vote in the first instance.

**(iii)** (1) **Presides** and maintains **order and decorum**; (2) **certifies Money Bills**, and the decision is final; (3) gives a **casting vote** in a tie; (4) **presides over joint sittings** of both Houses. (Also: adjourns the House for want of quorum; decides questions of disqualification on grounds of defection.)

marking_scheme.step: (i) Elected by members from among themselves
(i) Holds office for the life of the House
(i) Continues till the new House meets
(ii) Does not preside during the resolution

questions.stem_md:
Answer the following questions about the Rajya Sabha.

(i) What is its composition? [3]

(ii) How are its members chosen, and what is their term? [3]

(iii) Explain why it is called a permanent House, and name its Presiding Officer. [4]
questions.solution_md: Composition with numbers; method of choice and term; permanence and presiding officer.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(i)** Maximum **250** members: up to **238** representatives of the **States and Union Territories** and **12** members **nominated by the President**; the present strength is **245**.

**(ii)** State representatives are **elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies** by **proportional representation** with the **single transferable vote**; the twelve are **nominated** for special knowledge in literature, science, art and social service. Each member has a **six-year** term.

**(iii)** It is **never dissolved**; about **one-third** of the members **retire every second year**, so the House continues. Its Presiding Officer is the **Vice-President** as **ex-officio Chairman**, helped by an elected **Deputy Chairman**.

questions.stem_md:
India has a federal set-up with a strong Centre.

(i) Explain how legislative powers are divided between the Union and the States. [3]

(ii) Classify the following subjects into the correct lists: banking, agriculture, marriage and divorce. Give a reason for any one. [3]

(iii) Explain any two ways in which the Rajya Sabha reflects the federal nature of Parliament. [4]
questions.solution_md: Three lists and residuary power; three classifications with one reason; two federal roles of the Rajya Sabha explained.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(i)** The **Seventh Schedule** has three lists: the **Union List** (subjects of national importance), the **State List** (subjects of local importance) and the **Concurrent List** (both may legislate). **Residuary** subjects are with the **Union**.

**(ii)** **Banking:** Union List. **Agriculture:** State List. **Marriage and divorce:** Concurrent List. Reason, e.g. banking needs **one uniform system** for the whole country, so it is a Union subject.

**(iii)** (1) Its members are **elected by the State legislatures**, so the **States are represented** as units in Parliament. (2) Its consent by a **special resolution** is needed before Parliament can make a law on a **State List** subject in the national interest, which **protects State powers**.

marking_scheme.step: (iii) Consent for laws on State subjects
(iii) Explained as protection of State powers

questions.stem_md:
Compare the two Houses of Parliament.

(i) Give three differences in the way members of the two Houses are chosen. [3]

(ii) Give three differences in their terms and tenure. [3]

(iii) "The Lok Sabha is more powerful than the Rajya Sabha." Give four reasons in support of this statement. [4]
questions.solution_md: Three differences in choice; three in tenure; four reasons for Lok Sabha predominance.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(i)** (1) Lok Sabha members are **directly elected** by the people; Rajya Sabha members are **indirectly elected** by State legislators. (2) The Rajya Sabha has **twelve nominated** members; the Lok Sabha has **none** since 2020. (3) The Lok Sabha uses **first-past-the-post** in constituencies; the Rajya Sabha uses **proportional representation** with the single transferable vote.

**(ii)** (1) The Lok Sabha has a **five-year term**; Rajya Sabha members serve **six years**. (2) The Lok Sabha **can be dissolved**; the Rajya Sabha **cannot**. (3) The whole Lok Sabha is elected at once; in the Rajya Sabha **one-third retire every second year**.

**(iii)** (1) The **Council of Ministers** is responsible to the Lok Sabha alone. (2) **Money Bills** start only there, and the Rajya Sabha can delay them for only **14 days**. (3) A **no-confidence motion** can be moved only in the Lok Sabha. (4) In a **joint sitting**, the larger Lok Sabha usually prevails.

questions.stem_md:
In an imagined debate at Kalimpong Higher Secondary School, students asked whether the Speaker can stay neutral after being elected with the support of a party.

(i) State three powers of the Speaker over the conduct of business in the House. [3]

(ii) Explain three safeguards that protect the independence of the Speaker. [3]

(iii) Give two arguments for and two against the view that the Speaker can be neutral, and conclude. [4]
questions.solution_md: Three powers; three safeguards; two arguments each way with a reasoned conclusion.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(i)** (1) Decides **who speaks** and in what order; (2) can **adjourn or suspend** the sitting in grave disorder; (3) decides on **points of order** and whether a bill is a **Money Bill**.

**(ii)** (1) Removal needs an **effective majority** with **14 days' notice**. (2) The Speaker votes only to **break a tie**. (3) The Speaker's **rulings** on procedure **cannot be challenged** in the House, and the salary is **charged** on the Consolidated Fund.

**(iii)** **For:** the office has **strong safeguards**; Speakers often act on **established rules** and conventions. **Against:** the Speaker owes the post to the **majority party**; some decisions, such as on disqualification, may be **seen as partisan**. **Conclusion:** neutrality is **possible and expected**, and depends on the **conduct** of the person and respect for conventions (any reasoned conclusion).

questions.stem_md:
Some people call the Rajya Sabha a "House of second thoughts".

(i) Explain what this phrase means. [3]

(ii) Explain three ways in which the Rajya Sabha is useful to Indian democracy. [3]

(iii) Give two limitations of the Rajya Sabha compared with the Lok Sabha, and two reasons why a second House is still worth having. [4]
questions.solution_md: Meaning; three uses; two limits and two justifications.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(i)** The Rajya Sabha **re-examines bills** passed by the Lok Sabha. Its members, being **experienced** and less pressed by elections, can **debate calmly**, so hasty laws can be **revised**.

**(ii)** (1) It **represents the States** in Parliament. (2) Its **nominated experts** improve debate. (3) As a **permanent House**, it gives **continuity** when the Lok Sabha is dissolved.

**(iii)** **Limitations:** it can only **delay a Money Bill** for 14 days; the **ministers are not responsible** to it. **Worth having:** it **checks hasty legislation**; it gives the **States a voice** in a federal system.

questions.stem_md: Read the imagined news report from the State of Vindhyachal and answer the questions that follow. *(Imagined situation written by SOYL for practice.)*
questions.solution_md:
**(a)** Police is a State subject.

**(b)** Unlisted subjects.

**(c) (i)** Union law on a Concurrent subject.

**OR (c) (ii)** One advantage and one disadvantage.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** The **State List**.

**(b)** **Residuary powers**, which belong to the **Union** (Parliament).

**(c) (i)** The **law made by Parliament** generally prevails, because on a **Concurrent List** subject a Union law overrides a conflicting State law to the extent of the conflict.
